slides.narration: Welcome to this Spoken Tutorial on **API**.

slides.title: Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial, you will learn to,
• Define what an **API** is.
• Explain the role of an **API Key**.
• Identify components of an **API Request**.

slides.title: System Requirements
slides.narration: Here I am using a browser on a computer or mobile.

slides.title: Pre-requisites
slides.narration: To follow this tutorial, you should have completed Module 2: Art of the **Prompt**.

slides.title: What is an API? (The Waiter Analogy)
slides.narration:
What is an **API**?
An **API** is an **Application Programming Interface**.
It acts as a messenger for your applications.
Think of an **API** like a waiter in a restaurant.
You give your order to the waiter.
The waiter takes it to the kitchen.
Then, the waiter brings your food back to you.
Similarly, an **API** takes your request to a **model**.
It then brings the **model's** response back.
This response is delivered to your application.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing an API as a waiter taking orders to a kitchen (model) and bringing food (response) back to a customer (application).

slides.title: What is an API Key? (Your Restaurant ID)
slides.narration:
Now, what is an **API Key**?
An **API Key** is a secret password.
It identifies you as an authorized user.
Imagine it like your restaurant ID card.
This card shows you are allowed to order food.
Your **API Key** ensures only you can use the **API**.
It is very important to keep your **API Key** private.
Always keep it secure.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a key unlocking a lock, with a person holding an ID card, representing an API Key for authentication.

slides.title: Making an API Request (Placing Your Order)
slides.narration:
How do you make an **API Request**?
An **API Request** is like placing your order at the restaurant.
You send your instructions to the **model**.
This request includes your **API Key**.
The **API Key** is for **authentication**.
It confirms you are the authorized user.
Your **prompt** or instruction is also part of the request.
The **API** then delivers this to the **model**.
The **model** processes your instruction.
It then sends back the result.
slides.image_prompt: Illustration showing a user typing a request on a computer, with a key icon for authentication, sending it to a server (model) and receiving a response.

slides.title: Summary
slides.narration:
Let us summarize what we learned.
We defined **APIs** as messengers.
They carry requests and responses.
**API Keys** are identifiers.
They ensure secure access.
We also learned to make an **API Request**.
This involves sending your **API Key** and **prompt**.

slides.title: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now, for an assignment, think about other real-world scenarios.
Where might an **API**-like interaction be happening?
Share your thoughts on this.
